reconcile.note: Gill's standing explanation for gaps between the two registers, people staying behind, dying en route, or joining late, covers this family's ten-person shortfall too.

discrepancy.note: Paine's point that the two returnee rosters differ in their particulars covers the Delaiah-Tobiah-Nekoda entry's 652-vs-642 discrepancy as well.

quotes.text: Nehemiah, in like manner, gives a list of the returned families, and of the number of each family. He begins as in Ezra, by saying (vii. 8): "The children of Parosh, two thousand three hundred and seventy-two;" and so on through all the families. (The list differs in several of the particulars from that of Ezra.)
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Ezra 2:60 and Nehemiah 7:62.
